info.title: Hanzo Cloud API
info.description: Package form mounts forms (github.com/hanzoai/form) at /v1/form, the way apps/iam mounts hanzoai/iam: the module owns every route and every rule of a form, and this package hands it what only cloud knows.

get.summary: Reads the platform's settings of forms: every field type with whether forms may ask it and its bound, the limits every form and submission is held to (fields, hidden values, body bytes, submissions per address per window, webhooks), the sinks a new form takes when it names none, and the days a response is kept.
get.description:
Reads the platform's settings of forms: every field type with whether forms may
ask it and its bound, the limits every form and submission is held to (fields,
hidden values, body bytes, submissions per address per window, webhooks), the
sinks a new form takes when it names none, and the days a response is kept.
`saved` is false when nothing is stored and the defaults are in force.

SuperAdmin only. 503 when the settings store does not answer.

put.summary: Replaces the platform's settings of forms whole and answers them as stored.
put.description:
Replaces the platform's settings of forms whole and answers them as stored.
Every field type is listed once, enabled or not, each bound inside what the
store holds; every limit is inside its range; the default sinks name no field.
A type turned off stays answerable on the forms that already ask it, and is
refused on a form that adds it. The forms service reads the change within 30
seconds.

SuperAdmin only. 400 names every problem at once; 503 when the settings store
does not take the change.

A limit the document leaves out, forward and welcome among them, is the
default.

get.summary: Lists the caller org's forms, newest first, a page at a time; search keeps the forms whose title holds it and tag the ones carrying it.
get.description:
Lists the caller org's forms, newest first, a page at a time; search keeps
the forms whose title holds it and tag the ones carrying it. An org admin only.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page is the page, from 1. Default 1.

parameters.name: page_size
parameters.description: PageSize is how many a page holds: at most 200, default 50.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Search keeps the forms whose title holds it.

parameters.name: tag
parameters.description: Tag keeps the forms tagged with it.

post.summary: Makes a form in the caller's org and answers it as stored, its fields' ids assigned and its defaults filled: kind form, visibility public, language en, one question at a time, and the platform's default sinks when it names none.
post.description:
Makes a form in the caller's org and answers it as stored, its fields' ids
assigned and its defaults filled: kind form, visibility public, language en,
one question at a time, and the platform's default sinks when it names none.

A slug, when given, is the form's id for good: a second form with the same
slug is refused (409). Every problem with the form is named at once (400). An
org admin only.

delete.summary: Deletes a form with every response, webhook and delivery it has, and the webhooks' signing secrets.
delete.description:
Deletes a form with every response, webhook and delivery it has, and the
webhooks' signing secrets. An org admin only.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the form's id or its slug, from the path.

get.summary: Reads one form of the caller's org, by its id or its slug.
get.description: Reads one form of the caller's org, by its id or its slug. An org admin only.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the form's id or its slug, from the path.

patch.summary: Changes the parts of a form the body names and keeps the rest, then answers it as stored.
patch.description:
Changes the parts of a form the body names and keeps the rest, then answers it
as stored. The whole form is checked as it will be, exactly as a replace is.
An org admin only.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the form's id or its slug, from the path.

put.summary: Replaces a form whole and answers it as stored.
put.description:
Replaces a form whole and answers it as stored. Named by a slug no form has
yet, it makes the form under that slug, so a definition written twice is one
form: the way a seed states a form. A field sent with its id keeps it; a type
the platform no longer offers stays answerable where the form already asks
it, and is refused where it is new. An org admin only.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description:
ID is the form's id: 15 lowercase hex characters, derived from the slug when
the form has one, so a slug names one form for good.

get.summary: Exports a form's responses as JSON or CSV, a page of up to 5000 at a time under the same filter a listing takes; next is the page to ask for after it, 0 at the end.
get.description:
Exports a form's responses as JSON or CSV, a page of up to 5000 at a time
under the same filter a listing takes; next is the page to ask for after it,
0 at the end. The CSV has one column per field (its title), then each hidden
value, the respondent's address and kind, and when the response was landed on
and submitted. An org admin only.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the form's id or slug, from the path.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page is the page, from 1. Default 1.

parameters.name: page_size
parameters.description: PageSize is how many a page holds: at most 1000, default 25.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Since keeps the responses made at or after it, RFC 3339.

parameters.name: until
parameters.description: Until keeps the responses made before it, RFC 3339.

parameters.name: completed
parameters.description:
Completed keeps the completed responses (true) or the open ones (false);
absent keeps both.

parameters.name: query
parameters.description: Query keeps the responses whose answers hold it.

parameters.name: filed
parameters.description:
Filed keeps the responses on the CRM's timeline (true) or not yet on it
(false); absent keeps both.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Sort is submitted_at,desc (the default) or submitted_at,asc.

parameters.name: included_response_ids
parameters.description: IncludedResponseIDs keeps only these responses, comma separated, at most 90.

parameters.name: excluded_response_ids
parameters.description: ExcludedResponseIDs drops these responses, comma separated, at most 90.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: Format is json (the default) or csv.

post.summary: Brings responses made elsewhere into a form, keeping when each was made, a batch of at most 500 at a time.
post.description:
Brings responses made elsewhere into a form, keeping when each was made, a
batch of at most 500 at a time. Each is keyed by its external id (on a
subscribe form, by its address), so a batch sent again, or an import resumed
from any point, makes nothing twice. Each answer is read against its field as
a submission's is; a required field may be unanswered. With file, each new
response is also filed in the CRM at the time it was made; nothing is mailed
and no webhook is told. An org admin only.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the form's id or slug, from the path.

get.summary: Lists a form's responses, newest first, a page at a time: since and until bound when they were made, completed keeps the finished or the open ones, query keeps the ones whose answers hold it, and included_response_ids and excluded_response_ids keep or drop named ones.
get.description:
Lists a form's responses, newest first, a page at a time: since and until
bound when they were made, completed keeps the finished or the open ones, query
keeps the ones whose answers hold it, and included_response_ids and
excluded_response_ids keep or drop named ones. An org admin only.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the form's id or slug, from the path.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page is the page, from 1. Default 1.

parameters.name: page_size
parameters.description: PageSize is how many a page holds: at most 1000, default 25.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Since keeps the responses made at or after it, RFC 3339.

parameters.name: until
parameters.description: Until keeps the responses made before it, RFC 3339.

parameters.name: completed
parameters.description:
Completed keeps the completed responses (true) or the open ones (false);
absent keeps both.

parameters.name: query
parameters.description: Query keeps the responses whose answers hold it.

parameters.name: filed
parameters.description:
Filed keeps the responses on the CRM's timeline (true) or not yet on it
(false); absent keeps both.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Sort is submitted_at,desc (the default) or submitted_at,asc.

parameters.name: included_response_ids
parameters.description: IncludedResponseIDs keeps only these responses, comma separated, at most 90.

parameters.name: excluded_response_ids
parameters.description: ExcludedResponseIDs drops these responses, comma separated, at most 90.

delete.summary: Deletes one response of a form, and its webhook deliveries.
delete.description:
Deletes one response of a form, and its webhook deliveries. What the sinks
already hold (the CRM's timeline, a webhook's receiver) is theirs. An org admin
only.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the form's id or slug, from the path.

parameters.name: response
parameters.description: Response is the response's id, from the path.

get.summary: Reads one response of a form.
get.description: Reads one response of a form. An org admin only.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the form's id or slug, from the path.

parameters.name: response
parameters.description: Response is the response's id, from the path.

post.summary: Files a completed response on the CRM's timeline now, and answers the response with whether it is filed and, when it is not, why.
post.description:
Files a completed response on the CRM's timeline now, and answers the response
with whether it is filed and, when it is not, why. A filing that failed after
its submission is retried on a schedule; one a restart abandoned waits here.
Filing twice is one timeline entry. 409 for an open response, or a form that
files nowhere. An org admin only.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the form's id or slug, from the path.

parameters.name: response
parameters.description: Response is the response's id, from the path.

get.summary: Sums up a form's responses: how many were begun and completed, and for each field how many answered it, the distribution of what was said (choices, points, yes and no), the mean, least and most of a number, and how many open responses stopped in front of it.
get.description:
Sums up a form's responses: how many were begun and completed, and for each
field how many answered it, the distribution of what was said (choices,
points, yes and no), the mean, least and most of a number, and how many open
responses stopped in front of it. since and until narrow it to when the
responses were made. At most the newest 50000 are read, and truncated says so.
An org admin only.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the form's id or slug, from the path.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Since keeps the responses made at or after it, RFC 3339.

parameters.name: until
parameters.description: Until keeps the responses made before it, RFC 3339.

get.description: Lists a form's webhooks. Secrets are never read back. An org admin only.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the form's id or its slug, from the path.

post.summary: Adds a webhook to a form: every completed response is posted to its https address as JSON, signed with Hanzo-Signature: t=<unix seconds>,sha256=<base64 of HMAC-SHA256(secret, "<seconds>." + body)>; a receiver refuses a timestamp older than five minutes and an event_id it has seen.
post.description:
Adds a webhook to a form: every completed response is posted to its https
address as JSON, signed with Hanzo-Signature: t=<unix seconds>,sha256=<base64
of HMAC-SHA256(secret, "<seconds>." + body)>; a receiver refuses a timestamp
older than five minutes and an event_id it has seen. The secret is the one
given (16 to 256 characters) or one minted, kept in KMS and answered here
once. A form has at
most the platform's number of webhooks. An org admin only.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the form's id or slug, from the path.

delete.summary: Deletes a webhook, its deliveries and its secret.
delete.description: Deletes a webhook, its deliveries and its secret. An org admin only.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the form's id or slug, from the path.

parameters.name: webhook
parameters.description: Webhook is the webhook's id, from the path.

get.summary: Reads one webhook of a form.
get.description: Reads one webhook of a form. Its secret is never read back. An org admin only.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the form's id or slug, from the path.

parameters.name: webhook
parameters.description: Webhook is the webhook's id, from the path.

put.summary: Replaces a webhook's tag, address and whether it is enabled.
put.description:
Replaces a webhook's tag, address and whether it is enabled. A secret given is
kept in place of the one held, rotate mints a new one, and either is answered
once; otherwise the secret held stays. An org admin only.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the form's id or slug, from the path.

parameters.name: webhook
parameters.description: Webhook is the webhook's id, from the path of a replace.

get.summary: Lists a webhook's deliveries, newest first: each response posted, how many attempts it took, the last status the address answered and why it failed.
get.description:
Lists a webhook's deliveries, newest first: each response posted, how many
attempts it took, the last status the address answered and why it failed. An
org admin only.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the form's id or slug, from the path.

parameters.name: webhook
parameters.description: Webhook is the webhook's id, from the path.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page is the page, from 1; PageSize at most 200, default 50.

post.summary: Posts a delivery's response to its webhook again, now, and answers how it went.
post.description:
Posts a delivery's response to its webhook again, now, and answers how it
went. A delivery that failed, or was waiting on a retry when the service
restarted, is sent this way. An org admin only.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the form's id or slug, from the path.

parameters.name: webhook
parameters.description: Webhook is the webhook's id, from the path.

parameters.name: delivery
parameters.description: Delivery is the delivery's id, from the path.

get.summary: Reads a published form as its page draws it: the questions, the screens, the hidden values it takes, how it is answered and its theme.
get.description:
Reads a published form as its page draws it: the questions, the screens, the
hidden values it takes, how it is answered and its theme. Nothing about where
its responses go. No credential is needed; a form that is private, deleted or
never was is a 404.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the form's public id, "<org>.<slug or id>", from the path.

post.description:
Answers a published form. No credential is needed.

The answers are read against the form's own fields: each names a field (by
ref) once and carries the one value its type takes, inside its bounds; a
completed submission answers every required field. Hidden values are the
names the form declares. The response is from the signed-in person when there
is one (their account, from their token, never from the body), else from the
email field's answer, else from the page's visitor id.

Idempotent by token: the same token is the same response, so a submission
sent twice files one. With completed false the answers so far are saved and
the response stays open; a completed response is final and a later submission
under its token is answered with it unchanged. A subscribe form's response is
keyed by its address instead: one address is one subscriber.

A completed response goes to the form's sinks: the event stream, the CRM, the
forwarding address, the welcome mail and the webhooks.

429 past the platform's rate for one address, 413 past its body bound, 400
for a body that does not decode, a field no person fills, or any problem with
the answers (every one named), 404 for a form that is not published.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the form's public id, from the path.

get.summary: Lists the caller org's themes by name.
get.description: Lists the caller org's themes by name. An org admin only.

post.summary: Makes a theme in the caller's org: a name, four colours (#rrggbb), a font family and an https background image, each optional but the name.
post.description:
Makes a theme in the caller's org: a name, four colours (#rrggbb), a font
family and an https background image, each optional but the name. An org
admin only.

delete.description:
Deletes a theme. A form drawn in it is refused (409) until it names another,
so no form is left naming a theme that is gone. An org admin only.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the theme's id, from the path.

get.summary: Reads one theme of the caller's org.
get.description: Reads one theme of the caller's org. An org admin only.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the theme's id, from the path.

put.summary: Replaces a theme whole; every form drawn in it is drawn in the new one.
put.description:
Replaces a theme whole; every form drawn in it is drawn in the new one. An
org admin only.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the theme's id.

field.description: Field is the ref of the field answered.

type.description: Type is the field's type. Set on a read; ignored on a write.

company.description: Company is the ref of the field whose answer is the person's company.

email.description:
Email is the ref of the field whose answer is the person's address.
Empty, the first email field is. A signed-in respondent is always the
address their account holds.

list.description:
List is the CRM list the person joins, by name (a subscribe form's
mailing list). Empty joins none.

name.description: Name is the ref of the field whose answer is the person's name.

id.description: ID is the choice's id, assigned when empty.

label.description: Label is the choice as shown. At most 200 characters.

ref.description: Ref is how an answer names the choice; unique in the field, defaults to the id.

attempts.description: Attempts is how many posts were made.

code.description: Code is the last HTTP status the address answered; 0 when it did not answer.

created.description: Created is when the first attempt was made, RFC 3339.

error.description: Error is why the last attempt failed.

id.description: ID is the delivery's id; the body carries it as event_id.

next.description: Next is when the next attempt is due, RFC 3339; empty when none is.

status.description: Status is delivered, retrying or failed.

updated.description: Updated is when the last was, RFC 3339.

language.description: Language is the form's language tag.

mode.description: Mode is one (a question at a time) or all.

progress.description: Progress is whether a progress bar is shown.

csv.description:
CSV is the responses as CSV, for csv: one row each, one column per field,
then the hidden values, the respondent and the times.

filename.description: Filename is what to save it as.

items.description: Items are the responses, for json.

page.description: Page is this page; Next the page after it, 0 when this is the last.

total.description: Total is how many responses answer the filter.

choices.description: Choices are what a multiple_choice or dropdown field offers, in order.

description.description: Description is the line under the question. At most 1000 characters.

id.description:
ID is the field's id: assigned when a write leaves it empty, and kept
across edits by sending it back.

labels.description: Labels name the ends and middle of an opinion_scale.

multiple.description: Multiple is whether a multiple_choice field takes several choices.

ref.description:
Ref is the field's stable name, how an answer and a sink name it:
lowercase letters, digits, dash and underscore, at most 64, unique in the
form. Defaults to the id.

required.description:
Required is whether a completed response must answer it. A statement is
never required.

start.description: Start is where an opinion_scale begins: 0 (the default) or 1.

steps.description:
Steps is how many points a rating (3 to 10, default 5) or an opinion_scale
(5 to 11, default 11) has.

title.description: Title is the question as asked. At most 500 characters.

type.description:
Type is one of short_text, long_text, email, phone, url, number, rating,
opinion_scale, yes_no, multiple_choice, dropdown, date and statement.

validations.description: Validations bound an answer beyond its type.

answered.description: Answered is how many responses answer it.

distribution.description:
Distribution counts each value: every choice of a multiple_choice or
dropdown (with its label), every point of a rating or opinion_scale, and
yes and no.

drop_off.description:
DropOff is how many open responses stopped in front of it: this is the
first field they left unanswered after the last one they answered.

field.description: Field is the field's ref; Type its type; Title its question.

mean.description: Mean, Min and Max are a number, rating or opinion_scale's.

created.description: Created is when the form was made, RFC 3339.

fields.description: Fields are the questions, in the order they are asked.

hidden.description:
Hidden names the values a page passes in when it embeds the form (a video
id, a plan): lowercase letters, digits and underscores, at most 32 each.

id.description:
ID is the form's id: 15 lowercase hex characters, derived from the slug when
the form has one, so a slug names one form for good.

kind.description:
Kind is form (every submission is a response, the default) or subscribe (a
mailing list: an email field is required and one address is one response).

public_id.description:
PublicID is the address the form is answered at: "<org>.<slug or id>", as
GET /v1/form/public/{id} and POST /v1/form/public/{id}/responses take it.

settings.description: Settings is how the form is answered.

sinks.description:
Sinks are where each completed response goes. Absent on a write, the
platform's defaults are taken.

slug.description:
Slug is the form's own name within its org: lowercase letters, digits and
dashes, at most 64. Optional; once set it is the form's id, so it cannot change.

tags.description: Tags label the form for its org: at most 20, each at most 64 characters.

thanks.description:
Thanks is the screen shown after a submission, or where the respondent is
sent. Optional.

theme.description: Theme is the id of the theme the form is drawn in. Optional.

title.description:
Title is the form's name, as a respondent and the CRM timeline read it. At
most 200 characters.

updated.description: Updated is when it last changed, RFC 3339.

welcome.description: Welcome is the screen shown before the first question. Optional.

items.description: Items are the forms, newest first.

page_size.description: PageSize is how many a page holds.

total.description: Total is how many forms answer the query.

id.description: ID is the form's id or its slug, from the path.

saved.description: Saved is false when nothing is stored and the defaults are in force.

settings.description: Settings are the settings in force.

name.description: Name is who it is, for the greeting. Optional.

file.description:
File also files each new response in the CRM, at the time it was made.
Nothing is mailed and no webhook is told.

id.description: ID is the form's id or slug, from the path.

responses.description: Responses are the responses, at most 500.

answers.description:
Answers are its answers, each read against the form's field as a
submission's is; a required field may be unanswered.

at.description: At is when it was made, RFC 3339. Required.

email.description:
Email is the address it was from, when the source knew one. On a subscribe
form the address is the response's key: one address is one subscriber,
however many times and places it subscribed.

external.description:
External is its id where it was made: at most 200 characters, and the
response's key, so importing it again is the same response.

hidden.description: Hidden are values it carried, by the names the form declares.

source.description: Source is where it was made, at most 100 characters: commerce, a list's name.

created.description: Created counts the responses made new.

existing.description:
Existing counts the ones already held: imported before, or the same
subscriber.

failed.description: Failed are the ones refused, with why.

body.description: Body is the most bytes one submission's body holds.

fields.description: Fields is the most fields one form has.

forward.description:
Forward is how many responses one form forwards to its address in an hour;
past it the response is kept and not mailed.

hidden.description: Hidden is the most hidden values one form names.

rate.description: Rate is how many submissions one address makes in Window seconds.

webhooks.description: Webhooks is the most webhooks one form has.

welcome.description:
Welcome is how many welcome mails one form sends in an hour, counted apart
from its forwards so a flood of one cannot silence the other.

window.description: Window is the rate's window, in seconds.

identity.description:
Identity is who a response is from when nobody is signed in. claimed (the
default): an address typed into an email field is the respondent's CLAIM,
filed on the CRM marked unverified, on the person it names only when the CRM
already holds them and without changing them; it joins no list and is mailed
no welcome, and a list's consent is asked by the double opt-in instead.
verified: only a signed-in respondent (their token) is anyone; a typed
address is an answer and nothing more. A signed-in respondent is verified
under either.

language.description: Language is the form's language, a tag like en or pt-BR. Default en.

mode.description: Mode is one (a question at a time, the default) or all (every question at once).

progress.description: Progress is whether the renderer shows a progress bar.

visibility.description:
Visibility is public (answerable at its public address by anyone) or
private (not served there). Default public.

fields.description: Fields are the questions, in order.

hidden.description: Hidden names the values the page passes in.

id.description: ID is the form's public id.

settings.description: Settings are how the form is answered.

thanks.description: Thanks is the screen after a submission, or where the respondent is sent.

theme.description: Theme is the theme the form is drawn in, when it names one.

welcome.description: Welcome is the screen before the first question.

completed.description: Completed is whether the response is now submitted whole.

submitted_at.description: SubmittedAt is when it was completed, RFC 3339.

thanks.description: Thanks is the form's thank-you screen, for a completed response.

email.description:
Email is the address the response is from: the account's, else the email
field's.

kind.description:
Kind is account (a signed-in person, from their token), email (an email
field's answer), visitor (the page's visitor id) or none.

person_id.description:
PersonID is the CRM person the address is: the one key a response, a list
membership, an email event and an experiment share. Every event and
timeline entry the service states carries it, never the address.

subject.description: Subject is the signed-in person's IAM subject.

verified.description:
Verified is whether the respondent is who the response says: true only
for a signed-in person, from their token. A typed address is a claim.

visitor.description: Visitor is the page's visitor id.

answers.description: Answers are the answers, in the form's field order.

completed.description:
Completed is whether the response was submitted whole; false is one saved
part way.

created.description: Created is when the record was first written, RFC 3339.

duration.description: Duration is how many seconds lay between landing and submitting.

external.description: External is an imported response's id where it came from.

filed.description:
Filed is whether a completed response is on the CRM's timeline. A filing
that failed is tried again on a schedule, and POST .../file tries it now.

filing.description: Filing is why the last filing failed; empty once it is filed.

hidden.description: Hidden are the values the page passed in, by name.

id.description:
ID is the response's id: derived from the form and the submission's token
(from the form and the address on a subscribe form), so a retried
submission is this same response.

landed_at.description: LandedAt is when the respondent opened the form, RFC 3339, as their page said.

path.description: Path is the page the form was answered on.

respondent.description: Respondent is who it is from.

source.description: Source is web, or import for a response brought in from elsewhere.

submitted_at.description: SubmittedAt is when the response was completed, RFC 3339.

token.description: Token is the submission token the response was made under.

updated.description: Updated is when it last changed, RFC 3339.

page_size.description: PageSize is how many a page holds.

total.description: Total is how many responses answer the filter.

button.description: Button is the button's label. At most 64 characters.

description.description: Description is the text under it. At most 2000 characters.

redirect.description:
Redirect is where a thank-you screen sends the respondent instead of
showing itself: an https address. Ignored on a welcome screen.

title.description: Title is the screen's heading. At most 200 characters.

limits.description: Limits bound every form and every submission.

retention.description:
Retention is how many days a response is kept; 0 keeps it. A response past
it is deleted the next time its form is answered or its responses are read.

sinks.description: Sinks are what a new form routes its responses to when it names nothing.

types.description: Types are the field types, each with whether forms may use it and its bound.

crm.description:
CRM files the response on the timeline of the person it is from, or on the
org's own timeline when it names nobody. Absent, nothing is filed.

events.description:
Events states form_viewed, form_started and form_submitted on the
deployment's event stream: the form's ids and the refs of the fields
answered, never an answer's text.

forward.description: Forward mails every completed response to one address.

welcome.description: Welcome mails the respondent once, the first time their address answers.

answers.description: Answers are the answers, one per field at most.

completed.description:
Completed is false to save the answers so far and keep the response open
(a later submission under the same token completes it); true or absent
submits it whole, every required field answered. A completed response is
final.

hidden.description:
Hidden are the values the page passes in, by the names the form declares;
each one line of at most 500 characters.

id.description: ID is the form's public id, from the path.

landed_at.description: LandedAt is when the respondent opened the form, RFC 3339.

path.description: Path is the page the form was answered on, at most 500 characters.

token.description:
Token is the client's idempotency token for this response: 8 to 64
letters, digits, dashes and underscores. A submission sent twice under one
token is one response, so a double click or a retry files nothing twice.
Absent, the response is new each time.

visitor.description:
Visitor is the page's visitor id: letters, digits, dot, dash and
underscore, at most 64. It is who the response is from when nobody is
signed in and no email field is answered.

website.description:
Website is a field no person sees and no person fills: a submission that
fills it is refused.

completion_rate.description: CompletionRate is completions over starts, 0 to 1.

completions.description: Completions is how many were completed.

fields.description: Fields are each asked field's figures, in form order.

scanned.description:
Scanned is how many responses were read; Truncated says the form has more
than one summary reads (50000), and the newest were read.

starts.description: Starts is how many responses were begun: open and completed.

views.description:
Views is null: a view is stated on the event stream as form_viewed and
counted there, not kept with the responses.

background.description: Background is an https address of an image drawn behind the form. Optional.

colors.description: Colors are the theme's colours, each #rrggbb.

created.description: Created is when the theme was made, RFC 3339.

font.description:
Font is the font family the form is set in: letters, digits, spaces and
dashes, at most 64. Empty is the renderer's own.

name.description: Name is the theme's name in its org. At most 100 characters.

updated.description: Updated is when it last changed, RFC 3339.

items.description: Items are the themes, by name.

enabled.description:
Enabled is whether a form may ask it. A form already asking a type that is
turned off keeps answering it; a write that adds one is refused.

max.description:
Max is the type's bound: characters for short_text, long_text, email,
phone and url; points for rating and opinion_scale; choices for
multiple_choice and dropdown. 0 for the types that have none.

max_length.description:
MaxLength is the most characters a text answer holds, at most the
platform's bound for the type.

max_value.description: MaxValue is the most a number answer may be.

min_value.description: MinValue is the least a number answer may be.

created.description: Created is when the webhook was made, RFC 3339.

enabled.description: Enabled is whether responses are posted.

secret.description:
Secret is the signing secret, answered once: when the webhook is made or
its secret is set or rotated. Every delivery carries Hanzo-Signature:
t=<unix seconds>,sha256=<base64 of HMAC-SHA256(secret, "<seconds>." + body)>;
a receiver refuses one older than five minutes. It is kept in KMS and never
read back.

tag.description: Tag names the webhook in its form. At most 64 characters.

updated.description: Updated is when it last changed, RFC 3339.

url.description: URL is the https address posted to.

enabled.description: Enabled is whether responses are posted. Default true.

id.description: ID is the form's id or slug, from the path.

rotate.description: Rotate mints a new secret on a replace, and answers it.

secret.description:
Secret sets the signing secret: 16 to 256 characters. Absent on a make,
one is minted; absent on a replace, the secret held is kept.

tag.description: Tag names the webhook in its form, at most 64 characters.

url.description: URL is the https address posted to. Required.

webhook.description: Webhook is the webhook's id, from the path of a replace.

body.description:
Body is the mail's text: plain text, a blank line a new paragraph. At most
10000 characters.

subject.description: Subject is the mail's subject. At most 200 characters.

code.description: A stable token a client can branch on, when the refusal names one.

detail.description: What was refused, for a person to read.

bearer.description: The caller's credential, sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. It is either an access token minted by Hanzo IAM or an API key (pk-/sk-). X-Authorization, and HTTP Basic carrying the token as the password, are accepted spellings of the same header for clients that cannot set Authorization; a browser presents the session cookie instead. Every operation requires it unless it says `security: []`.
